# Exploring the Potential and Perceptions of Social Robots in Tourism and Hospitality: Insights from Industry Executives and Technology Evaluation

- Open access
- Published: 27 December 2024

- Ida Skubis ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-2447-9832 1 

## Abstract

The tourism and hospitality industry are undergoing a transformation with the expansion of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and social robots, aiming to enhance customer service, operational efficiency, and overall guest experiences. This paper explores the roles, customer service, operational efficiency, benefits, challenges, and personalization of social robots. Moreover, this study involves a detailed survey with 14 top executives in the tourism and hospitality industry, focusing on their familiarity with, attitudes towards, and potential adoption of social robots in their operations. The objective is to show the industry’s current readiness for technological integration and predict the future impact of social robots on enhancing customer experiences and operational practices in the sector. This paper explores the practical implementation of social robots in tourism and hospitality while forecasting their future role in shaping the industry. Using models like the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the theory of planned behavior, it examines how industry executives are responding to AI-driven robotics. By evaluating current applications and feedback from top-level management, this study contributes to both theoretical and practical discussions on how these innovations may drive operational change, enhance customer service, and reshape the service-oriented nature of the industry.

## 1 Introduction

The tourism and hospitality industry, characterized by its intensive service orientation, has always been at the forefront of adopting innovative technologies to enhance customer service and operational efficiency. In recent years, the emergence of AI and social robots has presented a new frontier for innovation in this sector. These technologies promise to revolutionize the way services are delivered, offering personalized and efficient experiences to customers while addressing the industry’s perennial challenges such as labor shortages and the need for high-quality service standards. This paper aims to present the role of AI and social robots in tourism and hospitality management, drawing on recent scholarly research to outline the benefits, practical applications, and potential challenges of these technologies.

Recent studies have demonstrated the diverse applications of social robots in the hospitality and tourism sector, ranging from customer service to operational support. Lee’s [1] investigation into the perceived benefits of service robots emphasizes their potential to enhance customer engagement through functional, hedonic, social, and empathy benefits. Similarly, Kang and Baker [2] highlight the transformative impact of AI and robots in designing customer experiences, emphasizing the role of technology in shaping the social servicescape. Labben and Burger [3] discuss the integration of intelligent robots in providing services such as information dissemination and customer interaction, noting the importance of social media in spreading tourist experiences.

Furthermore, the adoption of AI and social robots is seen as a response to emerging challenges, such as the need for contactless services post-COVID-19 [4]. Vishwakarma et al. [5] provide a comprehensive review of the adoption of social robots in service operations, indicating a significant trend towards their use in travel, tourism, hotel, and hospitality industries.

The integration of AI and social robots offers numerous benefits, including enhanced customer service, operational efficiency, and the ability to provide personalized experiences. Robots and AI systems can handle routine inquiries and tasks, freeing human staff to focus on more complex customer needs. Moreover, these technologies can operate around the clock, always ensuring service availability. However, the adoption of AI and social robots also presents challenges, such as the high initial investment costs, the need for ongoing maintenance and updates, and potential resistance from both staff and customers accustomed to traditional service delivery methods.

This article provides an exploratory analysis of the current role and potential applications of social robots in the tourism and hospitality sectors, focusing on the need to balance technological advancements with the indispensable human touch that defines these industries. Moving forward, the effective incorporation of social robots will depend on overcoming these obstacles, guaranteeing that technology serves to enhance rather than replace the human aspects of hospitality and service.

Moreover, the study undertaken in this article presents a detailed survey conducted with 14 top executives from the sector, including travel and tourism managers, hotel managers, directors, and hotel owners. The survey aimed to assess their familiarity with, attitudes towards, and the potential adoption of social robots within their operations. By examining the perspectives of industry leaders, the study seeks to understand the current readiness for technological integration and to forecast the future role of social robots in enhancing customer experiences and operational practices within the hospitality sector.

## 2 AI in Tourism and Hospitality Management

Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the tourism and hospitality industry is transforming traditional management practices, enhancing customer experiences, and streamlining operations, and reshaping marketing strategies. AI technologies, including machine learning, natural language processing, and robotics, have significantly impacted the management strategies within the tourism and hospitality industry [6]. The research by Saydam, Arıcı, and Koseoglu [7] provides a comprehensive review of empirical studies on AI applications in the sector, highlighting the emergence of themes such as anthropomorphism, service robots, and the evolving perceptions of employees and customers towards AI.

AI’s capability to analyze and interpret vast amounts of data has been a game-changer for personalized customer service. Machine learning algorithms and data analytics enable businesses to understand customer preferences and behaviour in unprecedented detail, allowing for the delivery of customized recommendations and services. AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants, available 24/7, have transformed customer interactions by providing instant responses to inquiries, facilitating bookings, making reservations, and offering personalized travel advice, thus significantly enhancing the customer experience [8, 9, 10, 11].

Operational efficiency is another area where AI has made significant inroads. From predictive maintenance and energy management to inventory control, AI technologies help in predicting equipment failures before they occur, thereby reducing downtime and maintenance costs. In energy management, AI optimizes the use of resources, leading to sustainability and cost savings. These applications not only contribute to a greener planet but also to the bottom line of businesses.

AI is optimizing also operational efficiency in the tourism and hospitality sector. Predictive analytics, a branch of AI, is used for forecasting demand, setting dynamic pricing strategies, and managing inventory more effectively. This helps businesses maximize occupancy rates and revenue, while minimizing costs. Furthermore, AI-driven robots and automation technologies are being employed for cleaning, service delivery, and even cooking, thereby enhancing efficiency and reducing the reliance on human labor [12].

In marketing and revenue management, AI tools off provide understanding of market trends, customer behavior, and competitive dynamics, which are invaluable for crafting effective marketing strategies and making informed pricing decisions. Dynamic pricing algorithms, for instance, adjust prices in real-time based on demand and other factors, ensuring competitiveness and maximizing revenue. Moreover, AI-driven marketing campaigns can target potential customers with highly personalized messages and offers, significantly improving engagement and conversion rates [13].

AI also plays a crucial role in staffing and human resources management within the tourism and hospitality industry. From talent acquisition and performance management to employee engagement, AI-powered solutions streamline HR processes. They can efficiently screen candidates, predict employee success, and identify areas for development, thereby enhancing the overall productivity of the workforce [14].

Despite these advancements, the integration of AI in the tourism and hospitality industry is not without challenges. Issues such as data privacy, the digital divide, and the potential displacement of jobs due to automation are of concern. Moreover, ethical considerations around the use of data and the potential biases in AI algorithms need to be addressed to ensure that the benefits of AI are equitably distributed [15, 16].

Looking ahead, the future of AI in the tourism and hospitality industry appears promising, with emerging technologies such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), blockchain, and the Internet of Things (IoT) poised to offer even more innovative solutions. These technologies promise to create immersive customer experiences, ensure secure and transparent transactions, and further enhance service delivery [17].

## 3 Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)

The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), first proposed by Davis [18] and Davis et al. [19], was developed as a tool to predict the likelihood of adopting new technology within a group or organization. Rooted in psychological theories such as the Theory of Reasoned Action (TRA), TAM has evolved into one of the most influential models used to understand human behavior toward the acceptance or rejection of innovative technology [20]. The model has become essential for examining how users form attitudes and intentions toward adopting technology based on their beliefs.

TAM is built on the idea that technology adoption and use can be explained by an individual’s beliefs, attitudes, and intentions toward the technology, much like the foundations of TRA and TPB (theory of planned behavior). The model posits that by understanding these beliefs and attitudes, it becomes possible to predict future technology usage when an innovative system is introduced. This predictive capability makes TAM valuable for organizations aiming to anticipate how new technologies will be received [20].

TAM specifically assesses the impact of four internal variables on actual technology use: Perceived Usefulness (PU), Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU), Attitude Toward Using Technology, and Behavioral Intention to Use Technology [21].

- Perceived Usefulness (PU) is defined as the degree to which an individual believes that using a particular technology will improve their job performance. It is one of the strongest predictors of technology adoption.
- Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU) refers to how effortless an individual believes it will be to use the system. While PU often has a more direct effect on technology adoption, PEOU plays a crucial role by influencing how users perceive the usefulness of a system.

The combination of these factors forms users’ attitudes toward using technology, which directly influences their behavioral intention to use the technology and, eventually, actual usage. TAM has proven effective in numerous studies for predicting how likely individuals or organizations are to embrace new technology.
